the last picture shows.desc: WITH FILMMAKER RUSTIN THOMPSON âWhy should we be upset about the disappearance of yet another cinema? Because it matters. Every theater matters.â â Martin Scorsese âA love letter to the movies.â â Aura Johnson, Director of Programming Ashland Independent Film FestivalÂ Ten states. 10,825 miles. 123 theaters. Filmmaker Rustin Thompson journeys into the American West on a search for traces of what was once a center of small-town life: the movie theater. On the trip, he finds long abandoned and forgotten cinemas; movie houses that have fallen into disrepair; theaters recently closed, theaters struggling to hold on, and theaters thatâthanks to their thoughtful caretakersâare not only surviving but thriving. Between the stops along the way, Rustin poetically intersperses excerpts from Peter Bogdanovichâs 1971 classic filmÂ The Last Picture Show , as well as reflections on past and present hardships facing the film exhibition industry.Â The Last Picture Shows is not only a timely portrait of an industry in crisis, one facing the headwinds of consolidation, streaming, and the diminishing theatrical experience, but it also reminds viewers that even in vast cinema deserts, there are oases of community and gathering that remain, where the movie house continues to be a place of wonder, contemplation, and connection. Director: Rustin Thompson (US 2026) 78 min.

late fame.desc: The great Willem Dafoe lends his delicate gravitas to the role of Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer (Edmund Donovan) appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attentionâand by the alluring presence of Gloria, the groupâs âtragic heroineâ (a sinuous, Kurt Weillâcrooning Greta Lee)âSaxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. This thoughtful, witty second feature from Kent Jones ( Diane ), working from a sly and hugely entertaining script by Oscar-nominated screenwriter Samy Burch ( May December ), is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York. Director: Kent Jones (US 2026) 96 min.

wild inside.desc: What would happen if a captive-born owl with no survival skills tried to make it on his own in New York City? In WILD INSIDE, we discover the answer is more incredible, and more consequential, than we could have ever imagined. A Eurasian Eagle-Owl named Flaco escapes from the Central Park Zoo and sets off on a magical odyssey through the island of Manhattan. Flaco overcomes his years of captivity and lack of survival skills to answer the call of the wild â and discovers he was wild inside all along. WILD INSIDE is an underdog story of resilience and self determination as Flaco the Owl beats the odds and accomplishes the impossible. Flaco busts out of his cage barely able to fly, but he adapts, he explores and eventually â it seems â he goes far beyond mere survival, becoming an internationally known icon of freedom, hooting from the highest water towers. He claims all of New York City as his wild kingdom. The remarkable story of Flaco raises some questions: is it right to keep a bird in a cage? Is there any real distinction between âzoo animalsâ and âwild animalsâ? How can we be better to our nonhuman neighbors? This one of a kind owlâs epic song is sung in WILD INSIDE by a chorus of besotted New Yorkers â young and old, bird-nerds and civilians, many of them immigrants themselves â all of them reaching for a glimpse of the wild, a glimmer of magic, or even just someone to believe in. Everywhere Flaco goes, he leaves that place and its people forever enchanted. Director: Penny Lane (US 2026) 95 min.

the rivals of amziah king.desc: Deep within the backwoods of rural Oklahoma, charismatic and musically gifted Amziah King herds a bluegrass-playing band of misfits while overseeing the premier honey-making operation in town. When Amziahâs estranged foster daughter unexpectedly returns, Amziah leaps at the possibility to renew connection and create a family business. But the honey game is ruthless, and Amziahâs rivals threaten to destroy everything he has built. Director: Andrew Patterson (US/UK 2026) 130 min.

the marching band.desc: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had â a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowdpleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe ( My Donkey, My Lover & I ) and Pierre Lottin ( The Stranger ). In French, English and Italian with English subtitles Director: Emmanuel Courcol (France 2024) 102 min

lake tahoe.desc: SATURDAY, SEPT. 12 â¢ 11:00 AM After crashing his family's car, teenager Juan spends a surreal day scouring the streets for help. Roaming from house to house, he encounters an eccentric mechanic, an aspiring punk singer, and a kung fu obsessive. Their strange worlds force him to face the grief he's been trying to escape. In Spanish, English and Italian with English subtitles Director: Fernando Eimbcke (Mexico/Japan/US 2008) 89 min

a song for the snow lion-theatrical prem.desc: This is the theatrical premiere of Â A Song for theÂ Snow Lion .Â In the high Himalayas of Bhutan, yak herders have long told their children that wherever there are glaciers, there liveÂ snowÂ lions, mythical guardians of the mountains whose fur is as white asÂ snowÂ and whose mane is as blue as the morning sky. It is a story that has taught generations to revere the ice and the peaks, and to understand that all life is bound together. When Yo-Yo Ma travels to Bhutan with his cello, filmmaker Pawo Choyning Dorji weaves Maâs journey around this ancient folktale with stunning cinematography. Together, they venture to the Lunana valley, one of the most remote human settlements on earth, where a young highlander girl still longs to hear the roar of theÂ snow lion, even as the glaciers that are its home recede before her eyes.Â A Song for theÂ Snow Lion Â is the untying of the knot of interdependence, a reminder that the survival of an ancient story and the survival of our planet may be one and the same. The song of the title is the beautiful ode to the yak and its herders at the heart of: LunanaâA Yak in the Classroom , the first ever film from Bhutan nominated for the Best International Feature Academy Award. A Bhutanese school teacher from the city is sent to a very rural village to complete his obligatory public service before he can leave for a life in Australia. This is an instant classic, a delightful neorealist adventure,Â a marvelous blend of serious and whimsical, with the special sauce of Bhutanâs astounding landscapes. Beautifully shot, with wonderful music, and a great cast of nonprofessionals (including the yak). Official Selection of the International Buddhist Film Festival Q&A with Director Pawo Choyning Dorji moderated by Buddhist Film Foundation executive director Gaetano Kazuo Maida A Song for theÂ Snow Lion Bhutan / 2026 / English, and Dzongkha with English subtitles / 21min / Documentary LunanaâA Yak in the Classroom Bhutan / 2019 / Dzongkha with English subtitles / 110 min / Drama Director Pawo Choyning Dorji (Bhutan)

la ciãnega.desc: SATURDAY, SEPT. 19 â¢ 11:00 AM The release of Lucrecia MartelâsÂ La CiÃ©nag a heralded the arrival of an astonishingly vital and original voice in Argentine cinema. With a radical and disturbing take on narrative, beautiful cinematography, and a highly sophisticated use of on- and offscreen sound, Martel turns her tale of a dissolute bourgeois extended family, whiling away the hours of one sweaty, sticky summer, into a cinematic marvel. This visceral take on class, nature, sexuality, and the ways that political turmoil and social stagnation can manifest in human relationships is a drama of extraordinary tactility, and one of the great contemporary film debuts. In Spanish with English subtitles Director: Lucrecia Martel (Argentina 2001) 103 min

antonio's road.desc: Its 1929. Antonio immigrates from Italy to pursue hisÂ dream as an artist in America. Mary leaves Ireland toÂ make a better life for her child. Their paths cross againÂ and again as they find their dreams crushed. With magical realism, we swing into the next generation, who chaseÂ their dreams, with jazz. Featuring the golden voices ofÂ Peter Coyote and Luciano Pavarotti and a cast thatÂ "moves you with poise, emotion, and remarkableÂ evocative power"Â Napoli nel Cinema Director: Donna DiGiuseppe (US 2026) 86 min. ANTONIO'S ROAD is a work of passion by a local filmmaker using many Bay Area shooting locations as listed below: The University of San Francisco, St. Ignatius Church San Francisco, The Belrose Theatre San Rafael, The Hibernia Building Jones Street San Francisco, The Museo Italo-Americano Fort Mason SanÂ Francisco, The Red Oak Victory Ship Point Richmond, Tivoli Decor Sausalito, Anchorage 5 Restaurant Sausalito, Fernwood Cemetery Mill Valley, Inverness.

once upon a time in venezuela.desc: SATURDAY, SEPT. 26 â¢ 11:00 AM On Lake Maracaibo, beneath the mysterious silent Catatumbo lightning, the village of Congo Mirador is preparing for parliamentary elections. For streetwise local businesswoman and Chavist party representative Tamara every vote counts, fought by all means, while for opposition-supporting teacher Natalie, politics is a weapon unsuccessfully attempting to force her from her job. And with her sharp eyes, little Yoaini sees her community sinking from sedimentation, her childhood and innocence with it. How can a small shining village survive against corruption, pollution and political decay â a reflection of all the flaws of contemporary Venezuela.Â In Spanish with English subtitles Director: Anabel Rodriguez Rios (Venezuela/UK/Brazil 2020) 99 min

american agitators.desc: SCREENING + CONVERSATION WITH DIRECTOR RAYMOND TELLES âI owe my life to Fred Ross. He completely turned my life around. Bringing Fredâs life to the screen is the medicine our society needs right now. He empowered people to be engaged in the democratic process.â â Dolores Huerta AMERICAN AGITATORS explores the remarkable life of Fred Ross, Sr., and a legacy of organizing that thrives today. Born in 1910 and raised in Los Angeles, Ross led a groundbreaking organizing approach that improved the lives of thousands. Beginning in the 1930s, Ross organized Dust Bowl refugees and during WWII he helped Japanese Americans find jobs and housing after release from the internment camps. After the War, in the face of KKK activity, he organized civil unity leagues in California by mentoring Mexican Americans and African Americans to build their voting power to challenge segregation in schools, which led to a successful integration of local school boards across Californiaâs Citrus Belt. Perhaps the most dramatic outcome of his early work occurred when Mexican American parents sued the Orange County school districts and prevailed in the Mendez vs Westminster case, laying the foundation for the Supreme Courtâs decision in Brown vs Board of Education. In the 1950s, 60s and 70s he worked with legendary organizer Dolores Huerta and the United Farmworkers Union. Generations of organizers and activists, many who are featured in American Agitators, stand on the shoulders of Ross and his innovative organizing tactics that cross sectors and issue areas. AMERICAN AGITATORS takes us to Atlanta Georgia where today âFight For 15â organizers fight for an increase in minimum wage and the unionization of workers across the Southern states. In Oakland, California in 2023, teachers, families and community members joined forces to forge a fair contract with the Oakland School District guided by the same principles of community organizing and getting out the vote pioneered by Fred Ross Sr. and set into motion by his son, Fred Ross Jr. Throughout his life Fred Ross dedicated his life to organizing and mobilizing people to challenge police brutality, fight segregation, and organize voter registration and voter turnout campaigns. He channeled anger and frustration into building member-led movements to change institutions and policies to improve the lives of ordinary people. He worked from the understanding that while protests can draw attention to create sustainable change, persistence and organization are required to build power and give people a voice in the decisions that shape their living and working conditions. AMERICAN AGITATORS tells a story of how today, collective action can combat racism, bigotry, and injustice and help move our nation towards a true democracy. Director: Raymond Telles (US 2026) 95 min.

the filmmaker.desc: SF writer/director JP Allen, and his company Coffee and Language Productions, celebrate their 25th Anniversary with their 9th feature film (of eleven), THE FILMMAKER.Â "Your identity has just been stolen." Â Â An isolated photographer returns home to find his apartment ransacked, his credit accounts compromised, and a bizarre recording waiting on his computer.Â Â Soon, he receives an anonymous phone call from a young woman seeking his help in committing a crime of revenge.Â Â This layered story weaves themes of identity, intimate secrets, and the shifting meaning of the past.Â Â Ashley Rain Turner, JP Allen and Rebecca deBoer star in thisÂ noir mystery .Â Director: JP Allen (US 2018) 80 min

the work in progress.desc: The Work in Progress Â invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about Americaâs ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community â and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country theyâre living in now and the one they still believe is possible. These encounters are intercut with portraits of Americans at work â in woodshops, laboratories, fields, board rooms, recording studios, theaters, and beyond. The message is simple but profound: America can work because, in many ways, itâs already working. And a central part of the work ahead is to reclaim the practices of dialogue, debate, compromise, and perhaps most importantly, listening, so that we might find our footing again. What emerges inÂ The Work in ProgressÂ is an unusual and provocative glimpse of America in its 250th year, and an invitation to all Americans to pull up a chair, invite a stranger, and lend an ear. Director: Ian Cheney (US 2026) 102 min

carter country.desc: Carter Country follows the two-year journey of America's most unlikely Presidential candidate Jimmy Carter and his small town that followed him every step of the way. This documentary seeks to capture the forgotten spirit of 1976, the last great Presidential election of the 20th century, when a small town in Georgia suddenly became the political capital of the world.Â This documentary is not the latest retelling of Jimmy Carter. It is the first telling of the community (his community) and their collective efforts that managed to lift up one of their own into The White House.Â Director: Bobby Buccellato (US 2026) 80 min

fallen angels.desc: Sparkling, dizzying, and deliciously potent, FALLEN ANGELS, NoÃ«l Cowardâs champagne-fresh comedy of bad manners, shocked and delighted audiences at its 1925 premiere. Two upper-class wives, their husbands away for the day, share a few toasts to their pre-marital dalliancesâwith the same man, who just may be en route from France to visit. Old rivalries and past scandals bubble to the surface in this intoxicating romp from one of theatreâs comedy masters. Starring Golden Globe-winner Rose Byrne ( If I Had Legs Iâd Kick You ) and Tony Award winner Kelli OâHara ( The King and I ), with Tracee Chimo, Mark Consuelos (making his Broadway debut), Christopher Fitzgerald and Aasif Mandvi, this new Roundabout Theatre and Tony Award-winning production of âpure escapist funâ ( The New York Times ) was filmed live on stage at Broadwayâs Todd Haimes Theatre and now comes to the big screen Directors: Scott Ellis, Annette Jolles (US 2026) 95 min.

sailing set her free.desc: SCREENING + CONVERSATION WITH FILMMAKER OLEG HARENCAR âJocelyn Nash is an icon for San Francisco Bay sailors. When I first moved to the Bay area, sailing 505s in the late seventies, Jocelyn was center-stage on the sailing scene â she served as a role model for me in both sailing and sailmaking. I have always had great respect for this phenomenal woman.â â Sally Lindsay Honey, National Sailing Hall of Fame Inductee, two-time Rolex Yachtswoman of the Year With the glamorous looks of a Hollywood movie star, a UC Berkeley education, and an upper middle-class upbringing, Jocelyn seemed to be on track for what was expected of a woman of that era. But she had other plans and veered off the traditional path to set her own course. That path came at a cost. Jocelynâs passion and mastery of sailing has helped pave the way for female sailors to compete in a sport that, only a few decades ago, was entirely male-dominated. Director: Oleg Harencar

one in a million.desc: âA Poignant, Decade-Spanning Portrait of a Syrian Refugee Caught Between Two Ideas of Home.â Guy Lodge, Variety Â âA Stunning Real-Life Refugee Epicâ â Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine âA coming-of-age tale where both the joy of freedom and tumult of assimilation test every family memberâs bondsâ - Jordan Raup, The Film Stage Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany â and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. This film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home? Directors: Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes (US 2026) 100 min

the art of adventure.desc: The Art of Adventure is an inspiring and deeply human documentary about the extraordinary lifelong friendship between world-renowned wildlife artist Robert Bateman and fearless biologist Bristol Foster. Through their epic 1957 journey around the world - armed with a 16mm camera and an artistâs brush - the film opens a vivid window onto a planet once wild and unscarred, and a bond formed through curiosity, courage and a love of nature. At its heart the film weaves together nature, art and activism showing how two very different men fought to protect the natural world: one through art, the other through science. Now in their 90s, Bob and Bristol still find sanctuary in nature. Their story is a moving reflection on legacy and mortality - and a celebration of lives lived with purpose. The Art of Adventure invites us to step beyond the familiar, embrace life with curiosity and heart - and never lose our sense of adventure. Director:Â Alison Reid. (Canada 2025) 86 min

giant.desc: GIANT, the 5-star critically acclaimed play starring John Lithgow (Killers of the Flower Moon, The Crown) as Roald Dahl, comes to the big screen. Winner of 3 Olivier AwardsÂ® including Best Play and a Tony AwardÂ® for Best Actor in a Play (John Lithgow), the production was filmed live in Londonâs West End ahead of its sold-out Broadway run. The stellar cast includes Aya Cash (The Boys, The Franchise, Youâre the Worst), Elliot Levey (Cold War, Patriots, Good) and Rachael Stirling (The Divine Mrs S). A world-famous childrenâs author under threat. A battle of wills in the wake of scandal. And one chance to make amends...Itâs the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl is making last-minute edits. But the outcry at his recent, explicitly antisemitic article wonât die down. Across a single afternoon at his family home, and rocked by an unexpectedly explosive confrontation, Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. Inspired by real events, GIANT explores with dark humour the difference between considered opinion and dangerous rhetoric offering a complicated portrait of a fiendishly charismatic icon.

italian wannabe.desc: SCREENING + CONVERSATION WITH DIRECTOR STEVE DABAL AND FILM SUBJECT BILL DISSELHORST Audiences are sayingâ¦ âReally something else, a humane masterpieceâÂ â John in Virginia âA beautiful film, and an incredible story of passion, love, foodâÂ â Lilli in CaliforniaÂ âWhen I read the description of this film I thought it was about food. But after watching it, I realize itâs about communityâ¦ itâs really about love.âÂ â George in MassachusettsÂ In a quiet village nestled in the Italian countryside, a celebrated Los Angeles chef begins again, not to escape his past, but to taste life again. In English and Italian with English subtitles Director: Steve Dabal (Italy/US 2026) 90 min.

the sun never sets.desc: Wendy (Dakota Fanning) believes she's perfectly happy in her relationship, until her older boyfriend, Jack (Jake Johnson), who is divorced with children, insists they take a break to make sure she's truly okay giving up on the idea of marriage and babies. During this time, Wendy unexpectedly runs into her ex, Chuck (Cory Michael Smith), who reignites her carefree and spontaneous side, and suddenly seems to want a family. The three of them navigate a chaotic, confusing, and often funny relationship triangle, reminding us that the pursuit of love is beautiful and messy all at once. The film was shot on 35mm on location in Alaska. Director: Joe Swanberg (US 2026) 102 min

coyote vs. acme.desc: Coyote vs. Acme hits theaters this week riding one of the more unusual stories in recent studio history — Warner Bros. shelved the completed film back in 2023 purely for a tax write-off, only to reverse course after major fan and industry backlash, with indie distributor Ketchup Entertainment finally rescuing it for the theatrical release it always deserved. That makes catching it now feel less like a routine outing and more like showing up for a movie that almost didn't exist. And it's a genuine showcase for the Looney Tunes: Wile E. Coyote finally gets his day in court against the corporation that's been blowing him up for decades, but he's not alone — Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Foghorn Leghorn, Porky Pig, Elmer Fudd, Tweety, Sylvester, Yosemite Sam, and Taz all turn up in a live-action/animation hybrid that leans hard into the classic slapstick chaos these characters were built for. Early reviews back it up too, with critics noting it's got as much heart as comedy and brings out the best in these legendary characters. Add in a strong opening weekend and a home-viewing release expected around September 29, and the case for seeing it in theaters this week is pretty simple: it's a rare live theatrical event for Looney Tunes fans, and the window to catch it on the big screen is short.

no country for mothers.desc:
Join us for a live screening of No Country for Mothers, a powerful documentary directed by Raeshem Nijhon and executive produced by Reshma Saujani through Moms First. The film explores why motherhood in America can feel so difficult - not because mothers are failing, but because too many are navigating broken systems without the support they need. From paid leave and affordable childcare to workplace expectations and caregiving, we'll be exploring the question: What would it look like if we built a country that truly supported mothers?

Afterward, stay for a thoughtful conversation. This is the kind of film you can’t walk out of without wanting to talk about it. We’ll open things up, then hand it to the room.

Together, we'll explore what needs to change, what gives us hope, and how each of us can help shape a better future for families.

Whether you're a parent, caregiver, employer, or simply someone who cares about the future of work and families, we'd love for you to join us.

shaun of the sheep.desc: On Halloween Eve at Mossy Bottom Farm, excitement turns to dismay when the clumsy Farmer ruins the pumpkin patch. Shaun tries fixing it with science experiments, but things go wrong when a wild beast appears in the woods.

peptide night - tiburon.desc:
Special Event - An evening on peptides: separating the science from the hype in 2026's biggest wellness story.

A nuanced crash course with Julius Ritter, founder of the California Peptide Club

Peptides went from obscure research compounds to dinner-party conversation in about eighteen months. GLP-1s cracked the door; a long tail of compounds most people can't pronounce walked through it. What hasn't kept up is the quality of the conversation — overclaiming on one side, blanket dismissal on the other, and very little in between for someone who's simply curious and wants a straight answer.

Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club, a private community of researchers, founders, and practitioners now expanding nationwide, and President of AGI House SF, a technical hacker house whose residents have gone on to build several billion-dollar companies. He previously scaled BASIS Health, a longevity food company, across two continents, was the first growth hire at Superpower, and exited an AI company. His work has been featured in Bloomberg, Business Insider, and The SF Standard.

The Science — What peptides actually are, what the (pre-)clinical data shows, and how to weigh the anecdotal reports that dominate the conversation.

The History, Zeitgeist & Future — How we got here, why peptides are having a moment, and what the space looks like ten years out.

The Protocols — What people are using for weight loss, longevity, hair, muscle, skin, focus, and mitochondrial function — and whether injection is really the only route.

The Sourcing — Compounding pharmacies, the research-use-only grey market, overseas suppliers: an honest accounting of what you're trading off at each tier.

Roughly an hour presentation followed by Intermission and Q&A. Come with questions — the format is built around them.

For educational purposes only. Nothing presented is medical advice, and nothing here is an offer to sell or supply any compound. Consult a physician before starting anything.

hope.desc: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung-ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

star wars: episode vi - return of the je.desc: In the epic conclusion of the saga, the Empire prepares to crush the Rebellion with a more powerful Death Star while the Rebel fleet mounts a massive attack on the space station. Luke Skywalker confronts his father Darth Vader in a final climactic duel before the evil Emperor. In the last second, Vader makes a momentous choice: he destroys the Emperor and saves his son. The Empire is finally defeated, the Sith are destroyed, and Anakin Skywalker is thus redeemed. At long last, freedom is restored to the galaxy.

star wars: episode v - the empire strike.desc: While the Death Star has been destroyed, the battle between the Empire and the Rebel Alliance rages on...and the evil Darth Vader continues his relentless search for Luke Skywalker. Widely considered the best of all the Star Wars films, The Empire Stikes Back is at 97% on Rotten Tomatoes!

star wars: episode iii - revenge of the.desc: Years after the onset of the Clone Wars, the noble Jedi Knights lead a massive clone army into a galaxy-wide battle against the Separatists. When the sinister Sith unveil a thousand-year-old plot to rule the galaxy, the Republic crumbles and from its ashes rises the evil Galactic Empire. Jedi hero Anakin Skywalker is seduced by the dark side of the Force to become the Emperor's new apprentice -- Darth Vader. The Jedi are decimated, as Obi-Wan Kenobi and Jedi Master Yoda are forced into hiding. The only hope for the galaxy are Anakin's own offspring -- the twin children born in secrecy who will grow up to become heroes.

rocky horror picture show - september 10.desc: A loving couple, a few lost monsters and a sweet transvestite from transsexual Transylvania sing and dance through a campy, sloppy salute to horror movies and sexual liberation. Bring your sense of humor.

the salt path.desc: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn, who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

to die for.desc: Suzanne Stone (Nicole Kidman) has always dreamed of being on TV and she's dead-set on making that dream come true. But there is just one obstacle: Larry Maretto, her husband (Matt Dillon). So, Suzanne convinces a love-struck teenager (Joaquin Phoenix) to get Larry out of the way for good. TO DIE FOR is the most critically acclaimed comedy of the year.

eyes wide shut.desc: At a Christmas party hosted by wealthy, unconventional Victor Ziegler (Sydney Pollack), provocative advances and innocent flirtations arouse suspicion as high-society physician Dr. William Harford (Tom Cruise) and his sexy wife, Alice (Nicole Kidman) watch each other from a distance. Alone later, this seemingly perfect couple confront their intimate sexual fantasies—which don't include each other. Caught between reality and illusion, jealousy and obsession, William struggles with his inner urges. Will he act on his erotic fantasies or keep them hidden deep inside? Sometimes a man can see more clearly with his Eyes Wide Shut. Stanley Kubrick directs.

bram stoker's dracula.desc: Gary Oldman, Winona Ryder and Anthony Hopkins star in director Francis Ford Coppola's visually stunning, passionately seductive version of the classic Dracula legend. In BRAM STOKER'S DRACULA, Coppola returns to the original source of the Dracula myth, and from that gothic romance, he creates a modern masterpiece. Gary Oldman's metamorphosis as Dracula who grows from old to young, from man to beast is nothing short of amazing. Winona Ryder brings equal intensity to the role of a young beauty who becomes the object of Dracula's devastating desire. Anthony Hopkins co-stars as the famed doctor who dares to believe in Dracula, and then dares to confront him. Opulent, dazzling and utterly irresistible, this is Dracula as you've never seen him. And once you've seen BRAM STOKER'S DRACULA, you'll never forget it.

miss congeniality.desc: For her entire life, Gracie Hart has dreamed of emulating the career of her mother, Emily, a highly esteemed FBI agent who died in the line of duty. Unfortunately, Gracie's aggressive nature has branded her as a loose cannon, and the only one in the bureau who actually believes in her is fellow agent and friend, Eric Matthews. When a terrorist threatens to bomb the Miss United States pageant, the FBI rushes to find a female agent to go undercover as a contestant. Unfortunately, Gracie is the only female FBI agent who can "look the part" despite her complete lack of refinement and femininity. She prides herself in being "just one of the boys" and is horrified at the idea of becoming a girly girl. To assist her with the emergency assignment, the bureau enlists the help of Victor Melling, an obsessive and pompous pageant consultant, to transform Gracie from a "woman without a detectable smidgen of estrogen" to "Gracie Lou Freebush," glamorous beauty queen. Transformation complete, Gracie must get comfortable with the mercilessly driven and perfectly coifed contestants, infiltrate the pageant and thwart the terrorists.

willy wonka & the chocolate factory.desc: The story of Charlie Bucket, a little boy with no money and a good heart, who dreams wistfully of being able to buy the candy that other children enjoy. Charlie enters into a magical world when he wins one of five 'Golden Tickets' to visit the mysterious chocolate factory owned by the eccentric Willy Wonka and run by his capable crew of Oompa-Loompas. Once behind the gates, a cast of characters join Charlie and Grandpa Joe on a journey to discover that a kind heart is a far finer possession than a sweet tooth.

nosferatu with live quarkestra orchestra.desc: Featuring an original live score by Denver’s own Quarkestra orchestra! Subtitled A Symphony of Horror and shot in the Carpathian mountains of Transylvania and in Germany, director F.W. Murnau's Nosferatu—an unauthorized version of Bram Stoker's classic novel Dracula—is considered by many to be the greatest vampire movie of all time. A long time ago in middle Europe, a decrepit, forbidding castle stood, casting an ominous shadow over the townspeople who dare not look upon it. The unholy dwelling is home to one Count Orlok (Max Schreck), an undead night creature with a taste for human blood. Into this picture steps Hutter, an unwary traveler visitor to the Count, with the deed for a property Orlok wishes to buy in Hutter's home town of Wisborg. That night, in preparation for the long sea voyage ahead, the vampire hastily loads his coffin aboard ship and waits.... Once at sea, Orlock bares his fangs and upon arrival in Wisborg, leaves behind a floating morgue. Now, preparing to feast on the citizens, the cadaverous count prowls the darkness as the eerie Nosferatu.
